chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rishi Basu
chunks.text:
Rishi Basu
A very good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining Infosys' Second Quarter Financial Results.
My name is Rishi, and I would like to welcome all of you. One question. Okay.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Prepared remarks
chunks.text: With that, I am going to hand it over to Salil for his opening remarks. Over to you, Salil.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
Thanks, Rishi. It is good to see that everyone listens to you so well. So good evening, and welcome,
everyone. Thank you for joining us. Our revenue growth for Q2 was 1.5% YoY and 1.2% sequentially
in constant currency terms. AI revenue was a standout at 10.5% of our revenue, growing at 29%
sequentially. And last quarter, it was at 8.2%.
Large deals were another standout at $5.2 bn for the quarter. This includes two mega deals. One of
these mega deals was for over $2 bn with a large international company for a period of seven years,
and this is net new. This deal is expected to contribute over 1% revenue growth in the coming
financial year.
The second mega deal was for $1 bn for a renewal. Our large deal pipeline is healthy and includes
some other mega deals in this pipeline. Operating margin was stable at 21%. Free cash flow was
strong at $928 mn (Editor’s comment) for the quarter.
As enterprises adopt AI at scale, another quarter of strong growth in AI revenues is a recognition of
our differentiated market positioning and client confidence. As an ecosystem integrator, we continue
to work closely with the frontier model companies, both open-weight and closed models. Our deep
investments in Topaz Fabric help our clients seamlessly navigate between models to ensure token
optimization and value realization.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
optimization and value realization.
Infosys continues to gain market share, especially where economics of the program is aligned to the
stakeholder interest. We remain the preferred AI strategy and deployment partner for our top clients.
As AI remains central to enterprise transformation in the years ahead, Infosys is well positioned to
help navigate this shift.
Based on our Q2 performance and revised outlook for rest of the year, our revenue growth guidance
is 1% to 2% YoY.in constant currency terms. Our operating margin guidance remains at 20% to 22%
for the year.
Thank you. And with that, we can open it up for questions.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rishi Basu
chunks.text:
Rishi Basu
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 3
Thank you, Salil. We will now open the floor for questions. Joining Salil is Mr. Jayesh Sanghrajka,
Chief Financial Officer, Infosys. The first question is from Meghna Sen from CNBC-TV18.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Meghna Sen
chunks.text:
Meghna Sen
Thank you very much. My first question is on your guidance. So, you have narrowed both the lower
and upper end. Could you help us understand why? Explain the margin performance, the benefit of
rupee depreciation, any offset and loss due to deflation, etc.? And did your salary hike also impact
your margins in the second half?
Third is, your AI revenue is 10.5% of your Q2 revenue. So how many deals won will have AI element?
And with AI jitters globally, is there a change in business? And fourth, how are your December quarter
furloughs shaping up versus last year and which sectors look the most vulnerable?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
Okay. Let me start off with some of them, and Jayesh will also jump in with some of the other ones.
So first, AI is really an incredible performance for us. It is 10.5% of our revenue, growing sequentially
29%. We had laid out the AI approach in the Hexagon with six different areas of focus.
And in this revenue mix, we see each of those areas growing well, especially things that we do where
we are building agents, where we are doing legacy modernization, where we are doing process AI,
where we are doing data AI. So those are growing exceptionally well, but all of them are doing well.
And then we have the partner ecosystem with that. That is really gaining momentum.
I think in terms of the global AI our attention is really much more on the large enterprises with which
we are working. So for them, this is starting to become more-and-more relevant. And with the
investments we made and build the Topaz Fabric and the capabilities we have, plus all the training
that we have done for all of our people, which many and more are certified now, ready to do work
with different partners of the frontier companies, that is where we are getting the good traction with
the enterprise clients.
I will spend a couple of minutes on the industries. I think what we see, and Jayesh will add more to

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
I will spend a couple of minutes on the industries. I think what we see, and Jayesh will add more to
that, we see really good strength on the Financial Services. We see good strength on Energy Utilities.
We see good strength on the Manufacturing. And we see some weakness on the Retail and we see
some weakness on the Hi-Tech. But it is a mix of all of those that we have put together in how we
see this.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
Jayesh Sanghrajka
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 4
So if you look at our guidance, our our last guidance was 1.5% to 3%. We had clearly called out at
1.5%, we expect even more uncertainty. Our Q2 has been softer and our volume continues to remain
softer. We have also seen pricing pressure on the back of competitive intensity and higher ask on
productivity. So all that is baked in, in our revised guidance as we look forward.
On top of that, as Salil said, some of the sectors, we see softness, Retail, Hi-Tech, where the
discretionary is lower than what we are expecting. So all of that is reflected in our guidance on the
revenue and which is where it is 1% to 2% now.
Our margin continues to remain at 21%. I think it is a strong performance on the back of all the efforts
that we have put in Project Maximus. If you look at last many years, we have been able to maintain
margins despite investment in business, whether it is sales and marketing, whether it is AI-led
investment, talent investments and all of that.
If you look at put-and-takes of this quarter, the margins have remained flat. We had 70 bps of impact
on post-sale customer support, which is a delta between two quarters. Last quarter, we had a
reversal. This quarter, it is an impact, so it is a difference in that. We had 20 bps coming from our

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
reversal. This quarter, it is an impact, so it is a difference in that. We had 20 bps coming from our
acquisition, it is a one-month additional impact last quarter to only two months of impact, so one
month additional on account of amortization, etc.
That was offset by tailwinds of currency, 40 bps coming from the currency, 20 bps coming from a
higher calendar and working days and 20 bps from the Project Maximus. So that kind of sums up
the margin walk.
As you look forward, the next half, which is H2, we will have impact coming from compensation, as
you rightly said, so that will have a headwind. We will see continued intensity on pricing. So we will
see that as a headwind. And we will continue working on Project Maximus to offset as much as
possible from there.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Mansee Dave
chunks.text:
Mansee Dave
Hi, good afternoon. So, starting with the guidance which is revised downward from 1.5% to 3% to
1% to 2% on a constant currency growth basis, how much is the weak demand and market pressure
affecting? And what has changed in the demand environment plans ahead, if I may ask?
AI monetization. Well, the AI as a percentage of revenue for Infosys this time is quite strong and
greetings to you all for that. AI is helping clients improve productivity, but it can also reduce traditional
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 5
billable work. So is Infosys managing to monetize AI-led opportunities fast enough to offset pricing
pressure at its traditional services business?
And lastly, hiring and productivity. So can hiring plans coexist with margin protection because there
are plans to hire around 20,000 graduates in FY27, if I am not wrong. How do you balance
investments in talent with margin discipline? Thank you.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So on the AI first, I think the AI revenues have been outstanding. As you pointed out, we have
exceptional growth in that. And that shows really how we have put together the AI approach within
Infosys, which is resonating with the clients and the six dimensions of the Hexagon in which each
area that we are investing and scaling up in, and then the foundation that we have built on the Topaz
Fabric that helps our clients.
So there we see many examples of projects that are going extremely well. These are scale projects.
Even in the large deals that we referenced, almost all of them have some component. One or two of
them have really full business transformation driven by AI as the fundamental element of the large
deals.
And that large deals has been quite exceptional as well, which has helped us in a way to give support
even for the next financial year with the expected revenue growth support that the large mega deal
will provide.
In terms of guidance, we continue to see what Jayesh was sharing in terms of the competitive
intensity. So there is the AI, which is giving us the growth. There is AI, which is also seeing the
compression, and we continue to see that.
There is competitive intensity because of that, and we have been extremely clear that we will only
take on the contracts where it meets our economic guidelines. And so with that in mind and all of the

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
take on the contracts where it meets our economic guidelines. And so with that in mind and all of the
margin work that is been done in terms of the initiative, we have been able to keep our margin at
this level. And that is what is reflected into our guidance where we see that competitive intensity and
the changes that are going on.
Now the macro environment is also equally in a place where there is continuing different wars. There
were some interest rate increases. There was also the 10-year yield, which is now neighbouring to
5%. And there is continuing element of tariffs, which creates a different type of an environment for
the global economy and therefore, for the type of clients that we work with, which is essentially the
Global 2000.
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 6
So all of those put together, we feel extremely good that the AI is going well, that the large deals are
good. And then we also see the competitive intensity in the market.
On the hiring, so first, we had 4,000 net increase in the headcount, which is very strong, which shows
that our continued confidence into the future. Second, we have 8,000 college graduates we hired in
the quarter.
For the full year, our target remains clear at approximately 20,000, so around 20,000 like last year.
And we have already done more than half in the first half of the year. So, we think this dynamic will

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
And we have already done more than half in the first half of the year. So, we think this dynamic will
continue in the way we scale. We are doing work, of course, in AI, the 10%, but we also do work in
other areas. And all of those areas are growing. That is why the hiring looks pretty strong there. And
then the productivity.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
Jayesh Sanghrajka
So just to add to what Salil was also saying on hiring, it is a function of what is the attrition that you
have, what is the utilization that you have and what is the demand in terms of volume that you see
and the productivity benefit. We have, give or take, 13% attrition. That means roughly 45,000 people
in a year, they leave us, and that needs to be backfilled either laterally or fresher. So, the fresher
kind of makes up a little bit of that. We are working at 85% utilization, which is, in our mind, very
optimum utilization. So, there is not much headroom left there from the optimization perspective.
And then there is a net new demand that you are seeing. And a fresher typically takes six to eight
months by the time we train them and deploy them to the project. So, we do have to plan ahead of
the time to make them, and that is the reflection that you are seeing today in the net headcount
increases. One more point on the overall guidance perspective. I think our guidance for the year
should be continued to be seen on the back of the fact that we did at the beginning of the year said
we will have offshoring impact of 1%.
We are looking at higher offshoring through the year. We did call out an impact of large deals with a
European manufacturing client, where we did not pursue the deal because it did not meet our return

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
European manufacturing client, where we did not pursue the deal because it did not meet our return
expectations. So, both of that put together impacted our overall growth guidance by 2% or continues
to impact roughly that. And it should be always seen in that context.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Chandra Srikanth
chunks.text:
Chandra Srikanth
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 7
Hi, Salil. Just wanted to get a sense on the guidance, but I do not know if it has been asked. Despite
a healthy TCV, why did you sort of narrow the guidance band? And secondly, this week, there have
been a lot of talk about cyber-attacks because of AI. And half of these cyber vulnerabilities are being
uncovered by employees or by agents. I just want to know what opportunity does Infosys see there
in terms of securing systems for enterprises, and what are the challenges going forward? Thank
you.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
I will start on the guidance. Jayesh will have something more to add on it. So what we are seeing in
the business today is very strong growth on AI, which was at 10.5%, growing at 29% quarter-on-
quarter and very strong large deals with one mega deal at over $2 bn, which is contributing to our
growth also into the next financial year.
That is then combined with what we see in terms of the AI productivity and competitive intensity in
the market, plus, as Jayesh shared, what we are seeing in terms of the offshore ratios, which are
changing with the changes in the US, India dynamic, plus what we see in terms of the choices we
are making where in the case of particular contracts, we are extremely careful to take the ones that
meet our economic thresholds and guidelines.
So, putting all of that together is where we put the margin guidance. Our attention really is to build
out at a faster and faster pace the AI activity, which is going very well with regard to the Hexagon
strategy that we have developed in each of the six areas and making sure that we are participating
in the large and mega deals, which are business transformation deals underpinned with AI.
That is the sort of deal that we won where it was something that our teams proactively identified and
pursued and then the client selected us. So that is the sort of work that we want to focus on. We

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
pursued and then the client selected us. So that is the sort of work that we want to focus on. We
know there will continue to be the productivity challenges that will go on, but those will go through in
some time period. The AI is here for a very long time where we want to build a very strong foundation
in that.
On the cyber part, the first thing, we have a strong cyber business where we are already working
with several of our clients in working to use some of the frontier model capabilities to ensure that we
are helping them to protect against or helping build agents which will protect against. Some of the
ones that have come out this week, we have some defences for which we are sharing with our
clients. If you recall, two or three months ago, there was another week or so where there was a lot
of this coming up with the new frontier model that had come out. And the same thing we had been
working very closely with that lab.
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 8
The one model before that, it was already with us, and we had built out the cyber defence with that.
So, it is a strong part of our business. It is something that we are looking to scale up even more. We
did a small acquisition, you may know, in the cyber in Australia a few quarters ago, which is also
building out very strongly because that is helping us to do things in an ethical way to make sure that

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
building out very strongly because that is helping us to do things in an ethical way to make sure that
we can unearth the vulnerability that the clients are seeing with the agents with this approach that
we are taking. So, we see some good growth in both of those areas.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Chandra Srikanth
chunks.text:
Chandra Srikanth
A follow-up, Salil. Would you draw parallels with what is happening with cyber with what happened
during Y2K in terms of the opportunity this opens up for Indian IT service providers? Will they take
up the work of finding vulnerabilities in existing systems? And can it potentially become a very big
business model?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So, I think the cyber one is a huge opportunity for Infosys. But the capabilities have to be very strong.
So we need to make sure we have built our own capabilities, which are both agent-based and
human-based combined and working with different frontier models, because each frontier model is
unearthing different things on the application layer, which needs to be addressed in a different way.
You may have seen in the recent ones where some of the government sites had to be redone and
so on. So those are things that we are working on, which our teams have an understanding of, and
it is a large opportunity. So, we think this will continue to be a growth area for Infosys.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Haripriya Suresh
chunks.text:
Haripriya Suresh
Hi. Good evening, gentlemen. One on AI revenues, I wanted to understand, I mean, obviously, it is
on a low base, but it is growing fast, and you have said that it will be half in the next two to three
years. How realistic do you see it because of how much deflation is in your traditional services
business? How do you see that play out?
And also after the PERM suspension and the changes that have happened with H-1B, do you see
an increase in talent retention and hiring costs in the US generally? I mean, over the next couple of
years, it might not be immediate, but as it goes forward. And on Hi-Tech and Retail, what exactly
happened? Because Hi-Tech this quarter, I mean YoY has seen quite a fall as well. What happened
in those particular verticals? Thank you.
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 9

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So on the AI, my sense is the growth, I think, is quite exceptional in the way the AI is building out.
And we see that being sustained. Now, you are absolutely right, it is on a low base. And it is a small
amount, and so there will be some volatility, but still growing very nicely over the coming quarters.
But it is not like every quarter will be exactly like the previous. There will be some volatility in that,
on a small base.
I think what we are seeing and what our attention is on is making sure that we fully deploy and
leverage that opportunity for our clients. And so, building out, for example, if you look at the
partnership network that we have, every frontier lab we are working closely with and they are working
closely with us. We are also working with open-weight model companies.
In Topaz fabric, there are 15 different models a client can take advantage of. We can do token cost
optimization and, of course, capability. Meaning, even the way we are doing, let us say, legacy
modernization, is changing quite quickly from what it was even 12, 18 months ago to what it is today.
So, all of that is moving at a rapid pace and that is our attention.
The second piece of the attention is really on these large transformation mega deals, which we feel
we are quite well-positioned on, where clients are coming to us, it is more something that our teams

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
we are quite well-positioned on, where clients are coming to us, it is more something that our teams
are working with them jointly and uncovering. It is not like an RFP that someone is responding to,
and making sure that is an AI transformation mega deal.
Then the continuing of the AI productivity that is impacting the revenue also goes on, and that will
carry on through the different parts of our portfolio. But at the end, that is for a finite time. Once it is
done, the productivity through the portfolio will be done.
So that’s something that we have looked at internally, but we are making sure that our focus on AI
growth is where our attention remains. All of that being said, that gives us more and more confidence
that the way we are looking at it for AI is where the clients are going for. And that AI transformation
is where we will work more and more.
A majority of the employees that we have in the US are local hires. So, we had already taken some
steps several years ago, which had brought us to this position. So, we feel we have a good like a
ratio in terms of bringing people on and in terms of cost efficiency. So, we do not see a change in
that. We will continue to grow that as that evolves. Having said that, in the recent quarters, we have
also seen our ratios changed between onsite and offshore.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
I will start on that, so we have seen different client situations both on the Retail and both on the Hi-
Tech. Hi-Tech, specifically in one. We do not see this across all of our industries. So, for example, in
Financial Services or Energy Utilities, or Manufacturing, we see really strong growth and
discretionary growth. However, in these two industries, we have seen some impact.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
Jayesh Sanghrajka
So, I mean, I think both Hi-Tech and Retail, like Salil said, we had some discretionary-related ramp
downs and some client-specific slowdowns in a way. Retail also was impacted because of the third
party, we had a larger third-party component in the previous quarters, which on a Q-on-Q, therefore,
shows up as a negative. So those were the impacts on both of that. I think from a geography
perspective, it has been broadly similar across the geography, at least Retail, Hi-Tech has been more
specific to the US.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rishi Basu
chunks.text:
Rishi Basu
Thank you. The next question is from Beena Parmar from The Economic Times.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Beena Parmar
chunks.text:
Beena Parmar
Hi, Salil. Just a follow-up on the cyber incidents. You know, you have large set of clients which are
Fortune 500 companies and also in the public sector space. What is the level of preparedness that
Infosys or companies like yours have? And do you also see IT budgets increasing given that you
said that you will plan to scale it up further?
Secondly, on the deal wins, the two mega deals were in which sectors? And since you, despite the
healthy wins, you still lowered the guidance, does it mean that the AI deflation is still continuing to
impact and, you know, when do you see that really going away?
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 11
In terms of the hiring, besides the wage hikes, I think, you are still seeing some impact on the
margins. Are you seeing any increase in employee costs, given that the hiring is changing, and also
looking at more specialized hiring and, you know, does that really lead to employee cost going up in
the next, say, few quarters?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So, on the cyber, I think there it is more a question of building out the capabilities that we are driving
to and scaling that up and so that demand will continue. We, like all organizations, are well prepared
sort of both internally and in terms of supporting our clients. But what we sort of share with our clients
is these are things that are happening new every day. So, it is not something you can predict of what
is the likely outcome, but it is better to be more prepared or also build out in these specific
vulnerabilities, agents and agent plus human which can address them, which is being done for many
clients. It is more a question of building out that capability.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So, the budgets of our clients will go up, but at the end, it is not like it will go up in one place. It is not
that overall will go up disproportionate, overall, will go up as a normal sort of a rate, but not
disproportionately because also they need to manage their own budgets in a careful way.
On the large deals and the guidance, I think the question on productivity and AI deflation impact. I
think we continue to see that, as Jayesh and I mentioned earlier, which is really multiple effects. One
is the effect of the AI productivity which our clients are seeing. One is the effect that Jayesh also
mentioned about how the on-site mix is changing. Another is the effect of the competitive intensity
and how we have been, I would say, disciplined in taking on contracts which meet our economic
guidelines and profiles. So, all of that comes together in this environment that creates what you call
the AI constraints or the AI productivity.
But the more critical element really is the growth of the AI, because that is a secular trend which is
here and the way we are now seeing it, this is a very fast pace of growth. And even with some
volatility, you are going to continue to see a very good pace of growth over the next several quarters.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Beena Parmar
chunks.text:
Beena Parmar
Compensating for the revenue growth, right? So, the traditional services growth. So, I mean, how
long do you see this really lasting?
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 12

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So, we have some internal views on what the mix of these two will be. But it is not something where
we are more focused on what the reduction is. We are really much more focused on where the
growth is, because that is going to stay for a very long time. Whether this stays for a short time or a
long time, we know that with that growth, over time, we will see the overall business in a much better
shape.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
Jayesh Sanghrajka
And if I can just add to what Salil was saying, while our large deals have been very strong, historically,
we have been on an average signing $3 bn of large deals. So that was always there in the guidance
that we baked in even earlier. The two mega deals that we signed, one of that was renewal, the other
one is a net new. And the net new is only going to ramp up from later part of Q4. So, in this year,
there is going to be a very minuscule amount of benefit that you will get from that deal. But the next
year, as Salil said earlier, it will, you know, contribute over 1% in our revenue.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
Jayesh Sanghrajka
So, look, we hire across the pyramid. As we have said earlier, even we are hiring at the bottom of
the pyramid, which is the freshers, and we are going to hire 20,000-plus employees over the year.
So, we are very conscious about what we are hiring and hiring the right talent to meet the right
requirement. And if you are hiring at a higher cost, automatically -- generally, it reflects in the pricing.
So, from that perspective, we do not really see a margin impact.
If you see last many years -- last couple of years, we have been able to maintain our margin at 21%
despite all the headwinds while investing in the business, whether it is sales and marketing, whether
it is talent building, AI talent or technology investment that we have done. So, we have been able to
offset all of that through very meticulous operational rigor.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rishi Basu
chunks.text:
Rishi Basu
Thank you, Beena. The next question is from Shilpa Phadnis from The Times of India.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Shilpa Phadnis
chunks.text:
Shilpa Phadnis
As much as Indian IT companies are denying any impact on PERM residency, if you can help us
understand, will it trigger a fresh wave of attrition for you in your primary market, client market?
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 13
Secondly, will your subcon expenses go up substantially on this? And my second question is around
as much as AI is driving productivity, do you think this will also lead to margins being squeezed in
your existing contracts?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So, on the first one, I think overall attrition number that Jayesh shared is lower this quarter than the
previous quarter in the range of 12% to 13%. We do not see any real impact on the attrition from
any of those activities. Neither do we see like a cost impact because we already have within the US,
a mix where the majority of the people are local hires. And that is something that has been in motion
for several years. So that is something that we feel good about how we can bring in more people
and how we can maintain delivery excellence with our clients with that sort of a team. The second
one?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
Yes. On the margin, I think what we see is there is a tremendous sort of desire from clients to have
the AI create a benefit in terms of productivity for their activities, for their work that we do with them.
And we know that many of those things, based on the investments we made, we can make it real
for our clients. So given the investments we made in things like Topaz Fabric, we can make those
benefits real for the clients while maintaining, as we have done over the last several quarters, the
margin profile without doing any other activity below the line and so on.
We are very much focused on making sure that the productivity benefit we derive from AI and that it
matches to what the clients are asking. Now there are sometimes asks that are much higher than
what we can derive from the AI productivity, which is where we say that it does’nt fit our economic
profile. So we are much more disciplined about that.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Shilpa Phadnis
chunks.text:
Shilpa Phadnis
Last question. As much as you are doubling down on GCCs, how far are you from $1 bn milestones?
And second, it involves a lot of upfront investments from your side; people, software, takeovers. So,
if you can help us understand where you are on that journey?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 14
GCCs is an incredible growth area. I think this current phase, we announced, I think, just last week,
a very large financial services client publicly discussing our work we have done with them on the AI
GCC. So there, what is happening is many GCCs have been being built for many years by different
companies. And in the last two, three years, there has been an increased push of the AI infusion into
the GCC itself.
And that is where we have built an even stronger specialization where we can help if you have built
the GCC five, seven years ago to help you to transform it and if you are building it now to help you
to create it with that AI inside it, because the recruitment is different, the training is different. The type
of people are different, the pyramids are different. So, we have an ability to build and scale that up
and which is why clients are working with us more and more where the GCC business is growing
quite nicely for us.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rishi Basu
chunks.text:
Rishi Basu
Thank you, Shilpa. The next question is from Poulomi Chatterjee from the Financial Express.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Poulomi Chatterjee
chunks.text:
Poulomi Chatterjee
Good evening. I am just curious, I mean, you have underlined the high competitive pressure when it
comes to large deals. Do you have any intention of entering the mid-market? There is some of your
peers who are already turning their focus to the segment. And also with regards to your FDE team,
you had shared a target of 6,000. Like I am curious what is the progress on this? And what proportion
of your hiring do these roles comprise of currently?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
On the first one, we typically work with companies, enterprises, organizations, which have a huge
need for some level of technology transformation. It so happens that many of them are large
organizations because they have complex needs. But even today and even in the past, we have
always worked with organizations which are not only large, which can also benefit from these
activities, and that will continue. So there are several examples of that, which are long-standing
clients of Infosys.
The predominant focus is large companies because they have that large need for the tech
transformation. On the FDEs, the progress is strong. We are also building the internal with the
training, and we are also going with the external with the recruitment and it is progressing along.
What I think we had shared was the 6,000 was over the multiple years, and that is exactly how the
planning is going right now.
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 15

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rishi Basu
chunks.text:
Rishi Basu
Thank you. The next question is from Uma Kannan from the Deccan Herald.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Uma Kannan
chunks.text:
Uma Kannan
Hi good evening. Salil, you did speak about cyber security, but mine is very specific. This is regarding
eMudhra breach. You are using eMudhra solutions, if I am not wrong. I think so. Though eMudhra
said the incident has no connection with its e-sign services, what kind of measures are you taking?
Can you explain a bit more about it? And will you be migrating to other certified providers in the wake
of this incident?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So there, I do not have any specific comments on it right now. I have to look into it a little bit more
depth and come back to you.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Uma Kannan
chunks.text:
Uma Kannan
Okay. So, this is with regards to North America and India market. It is kind of your revenue, if I look
at in Q2, it has come down. Any specific reasons? And how H2 will be for you in FY27?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
Jayesh Sanghrajka
So, if you look at India, this quarter, the revenue has actually gone up. And typically, there is a little
bit of a seasonality because one of our contracts, you do get revenue. It is related to the returns,
etc., that is being filed in the quarter. The US has been softer over the last few quarters, and that is
pretty much of the industry phenomena. The Europe and the rest of the market has been stronger.
And when you look at the growth from that perspective, US generally has that. And then there are
nuances, like we said earlier, one of the sectors, which is Hi-Tech slowdown was from a specific
client in the US because the client was looking at ramping down, etc. So, all of that does impact

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Uma Kannan
chunks.text:
Uma Kannan
One more question. Last time, you said 80,000 employees are working on coding tools. I mean, what
is it happening now? Like are there any increase in numbers?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 16
Yes. So that number is increasing. Also, what we are doing is the certification numbers are going up,
the people who are getting trained are going up. Our partnerships with the frontier model companies
are going up. So, the large two frontier models plus new ones, which are both cloud and frontier
models plus the open-weight model companies, all of that is expanding. We had given that as like
one example, but those numbers are all growing in the terms of the work we are doing.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jas Bardia
chunks.text:
Jas Bardia
Hi. Good evening. Just a couple of questions. So, if I look at the Q2 guidance that the company has
issued this quarter, if we look at the guidance issued during the second quarter, it is, I think, the
weakest in seven years for the full year, that is. If I do the math, it points towards the fact that the
company might grow at its lowest pace in at least three years in FY27. So, in the short term,
considering there are furloughs in the second half, the mega deal ramps up next year and also that
there is pricing competition for large deals.
So, what is the company doing to sort of arrest this slowing growth? Second, with reference to your
ambitions on the AI work in the next three years that Infosys expects to get, do you expect a lot of
this AI spending to come from -- to be net new? Or do you expect it to come from existing IT budgets?
If you can just throw a little more light on that? And second, in continuation to this question, what will
the impact be on the company's margins?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So, on the first, I think what we are doing in terms of where the attention is in revenue and growth is
focused essentially on what we are seeing as the large opportunity for AI services. We shared a few
months ago that this opportunity is approximately $300 bn addressable market. We identified six
broad areas. And then we started to make sure that we invest in building the capability, training our
people and building the partnerships to make that whole ecosystem work, the foundation of which is
Fabric.
Then that growth is now looking very good. So that part is moving quite well. What we are also
seeing, as you pointed out, is that there is the AI productivity benefits that clients are looking at, and
that is also impacting other parts of our business. So, we want to make sure that the first continues
to grow well, and we continue to be the leaders with investment.
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 17
And the second, we want to make sure that we have the tools to support it because at the end, it is
a finite process because once you finish with all the work that you are doing through productivity, it
is done. And so that is important. But the real critical thing is where does the AI growth go, because
that is where the leadership comes in terms of what the market and what the clients are looking for.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
that is where the leadership comes in terms of what the market and what the clients are looking for.
And so that is the way we are looking at it. We will see over time how this develops. The other point
that we are focusing on is what you described the mega deals, the large deals because there, where
we are doing business transformation, AI-led work, other consolidation, other cost work, that is work
that gives us more support for the future in terms of the growth, which is what we shared that this
mega deal will give us -- it is estimated to give us about 1% of growth next year.
So, there are two big dimensions, AI, which is a very long-term secular trend. The mega deals, which
we have a unique positioning on because we believe with the business transformation and
something which we can help craft that we are well positioned. And then, of course, there is the finite
amount, which will go through in the productivity.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
On the margins, what I think we have done is the program that we started some years ago that
Jayesh has led, which is working very well. That is part of the reason that we have maintained our
margin. In fact, last year, I think we increased our margins from that. And there is a continuous
attention upon making sure that we are taking contracts from clients which meet our economic
guidelines.
So that has obviously an impact that we do not take every contract, but it also has the impact that
our margins are better protected. And therefore, you see, I would say, fairly consistent margin over
the last several quarters even as the industry has seen some wobbles. And we have a very strong
cash flow generation machine, which has produced this quarter over $900 mn. So that is like more
supporting of the fact that our margin is a real margin.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rishi Basu
chunks.text:
Rishi Basu
Thank you, Jas. The next question is from Sanjana from The Hindu Businessline.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Sanjana B
chunks.text:
Sanjana B
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 18
Good evening, gentlemen. Can you give us an update on the North America market? I think it has
seen some softness during the quarter. Any factors to sort of explain this? And also, Jayesh, you
mentioned that you are ramping up your offshore presence. Can you talk a little bit about that? Which
countries are you exploring?
And recently, many smaller GCCs in India have shut shop because of issues related to scaling. Have
you seen instances where a lot of these companies have come back to outsource their work to IT
services companies like yourself? Thanks.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So, let me start with the second one and then the geography and margin, Jayesh will answer. On
the GCCs, I think our approach has been to work with the GCCs to help them scale up, do a big AI
transformation or build the new AI ones as they are coming online. There have been companies that,
as you mentioned, are looking to do something different with their GCCs, and we are also in
discussions with some of those where we can either help them or either we can take them and
transform them. And those are ongoing discussions that are there.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
Jayesh Sanghrajka
On the segments, if you look at North America, as I said earlier, there have been certain segments
which were impacted because of the lower discretionary spend and the client-specific ramp downs
that were mainly from North America, and therefore, you see a softness in North America. At the
same time, other segments like Europe and rest of the world has done really well for us. So that is
a balance there. In terms of offshoring, most of our offshoring is to India. We do use some of the
nearshore locations at times Mexico, Canada, etc. But when we talk about offshoring, it is always
towards India.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rukmini Rao
chunks.text:
Rukmini Rao
Sure, thank you. Jayesh, one, if you are looking at the cost of technical subcontracting probably from
H1 of last year to H1 of this year, it is about 15%, 16% or so increase. So, would it be fair if we are
to look at the AI growth story at Infosys, would a lot of this be fair enough to sort of infer that it is from
AI-related technical sub costs that are coming up?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
Jayesh Sanghrajka
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 19
No. On the contrary, technical subcontractor as a percentage of revenue has remained in the range
of 8.9% of the revenue for most of the year, last year as well as this year. So, it has been between
8% to 9% of the revenue, and we expect it to remain in the same range.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rukmini Rao
chunks.text:
Rukmini Rao
But Jayesh, just to understand, if the subcontracting costs are going up and if this is related to AI
kind of deals that you may require, what I wanted to understand is if you are actually training a lot of
people on the AI side, where is this, you know, the need of expertise coming in from? And if Infosys
has to fill this gap, would you be -- looking at probably an acquisition, which might be a lot more
sensible if there is a long-term kind of engagement that you would be looking at?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
Jayesh Sanghrajka
No. So look, subcontractors for us has been in this range for a long period of time. There are multiple
reasons why it is because at times, you need certain skills in certain geography for a short period of
time, right? At times, you need certain skills immediately by the time you ramp up the projects and -
- or you hire the people, there is a lead time to hire people, but the client expects somebody to be
on the project immediately. And then you get subcontractors, deploy them on the project.
And then over a period of time, once you hire somebody, you replace that. So that is a process that
goes and it is a whole planning cycle that goes behind how and what kind of subcontractors need
and where are they needed. And that is it. I do not think it is so much about only AI, which has led to
the subcontractor. It has been there even a pre-AI days, our subcontractor has been between around
8% for a long period of time.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rukmini Rao
chunks.text:
Rukmini Rao
Salil, also in terms of the whole AI story that we are looking at, for you, when it comes to margins
from this incremental AI plug-ins probably in existing contracts that are coming up or even new AI
contracts, some sense of how do you see these margins from especially AI-led deals sort of heading
towards? And is this what you are probably banking on to sort of defend your margins if, let us say,
pricing pressure or external uncertainties sort of continue for the next 12 or 18 months or we do not
know how. So, is that something that you are banking on to protect your margins?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So, on the AI, we first do not disclose the margin externally separately on the AI versus the other
type of projects. Having said that, we are very comfortable with how the clients are seeing the value
that we are providing on the AI. And so we are good with where that is going. The margin of the
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 20
company overall, not just the AI, we are very comfortable with the guidance of 20% to 22%, which
has been consistent for a number of years now. And we see that as critical and important.
And in fact, our whole attention of the margin program is, as we see the macro changing and other
factors stabilizing, this becomes supporting our ambition that margin should be premier in this
approach. So, we feel good about the margin guidance.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rukmini Rao
chunks.text:
Rukmini Rao
Overall, Salil, if you have to look at future, do you see AI projects coming up in better margins for
you given that one of your peers already said that AI projects are coming at a better margin for them.
So just to understand how you stand.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So, I do not know about the other comment. But for us, the margin of the AI versus the non-AI, we
are not externally sharing. However, the overall margin of the company is very high. And so you
could see some people whose margins are low overall might have a different view.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rishi Basu
chunks.text:
Rishi Basu
Thank you, Rukmini. The next question is from Pooja Patil from Businessworld.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Good evening. There is definitely an AI-related revenue growth that we are seeing. But I wanted to
chunks.text:
Good evening. There is definitely an AI-related revenue growth that we are seeing. But I wanted to
understand that how much of this represents genuinely incremental business rather than existing
services being reclassified or replaced by AI-led delivery. Also, is AI beginning to put pressure on the
traditional billing and pricing models? And one more question with regard to dividend is that what
factors determine this INR26 interim dividend, particularly with the company lowering its revenue
growth? And how is Infosys balancing shareholder returns with investments in AI capabilities,
acquisitions and talent?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
I think what we see on that is that the AI revenue growth continues with a lot of strength. It is not
something which is replacing what we have. There is a lot of new work that we are doing. For
example, one of the areas among those six which are growing well is where we do work on
modernizing a client's environment using AI capability. That is new work. It is not that that was
something that we were doing in the past. And so the approach we have taken is the work has to fit
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 21
into one of those six areas, and that is the work then that we share outside at this 10.5%, which is
growing quite well.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Pooja Patil
chunks.text:
Pooja Patil
The dividend one. What factors led to this much? And how is the company planning, especially with
the lowering revenue growth?

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
Jayesh Sanghrajka
So, I think if you look at our capital allocation policy that we rolled out almost two years back, we had
very clearly said that 85% of the free cash flow that we generate, we will return back to shareholders
over a five-year period. It will be a combination of dividend and buyback. And within that, it will be a
progressively increasing dividend. So, we have already committed what is the money that we will
pay back to shareholders over a five-year period, right? And we are executing on that.
Last year's final dividend (Editor’s comment) was INR25, and therefore, we have increased that from
that to INR26 now. And we are just executing on that at this point in time. We have had a robust cash
flow generation, as Salil said. So, all of that is reflecting in the increasing dividend that the Board
has recommended.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Rishi Basu
chunks.text:
Rishi Basu
Thank you. With that, we come to the end of this press conference. Thank you, our friends from
media. Thank you, Salil. Thank you, Jayesh.
Before we conclude, please note that the archived webcast of this press conference will be available

outside. Thank you and have a very good evening.

Salil Parekh
Thanks, Sandeep. Good evening and good morning to everyone on the call. Thank you for joining

Our revenue growth for Q2 was at 1.5% YoY and 1.2% sequentially in constant currency terms. Our

Our large deals were another standout at $5.2 bn for the quarter. This includes two mega deals. One

External Document © 2026 Infosys Limited 2
As enterprises adopt AI at scale, another quarter of strong growth in AI revenues is a recognition of
our differentiated market positioning and client confidence. We are advising large global enterprises
on their AI strategy and continue to invest in deep domain and technology capabilities to bring new
ideas and an integrated ecosystem to help businesses unlock AI value at scale.
A premier food services company was processing over 10,000 invoices a day across siloed systems,

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
A premier food services company was processing over 10,000 invoices a day across siloed systems,
which made approval, disputes and payment tracking difficult. The new solution had to leave existing
legacy systems running undisturbed. We used AI to turn business requirements directly into working
software and built a single invoicing platform alongside the old systems. The result was 40% faster
time to market, 80% less rework and 30% more defects caught before go-live.
In another example, by embedding AI agents into the software modernization lifecycle, we helped
an education technology company modernize its aging platform with significantly lower risk and
effort, achieving 40% effort reduction and a production ready solution.
As an ecosystem integrator, we continue to work closely with frontier model companies, including
both open weight and closed models. Our deep investments in Topaz Fabric help our clients
seamlessly navigate between models to ensure token optimization and value realization.
Infosys continues to gain market share, especially where economics of the program is aligned to the
stakeholder interest. We remain the preferred AI strategy and deployment partner for our top clients.

chunks.text:
Jayesh Sanghrajka
Thank you, Salil. Good morning, good evening, everyone and thank you for joining the call today.
Let me begin with some comments about the broader environment. Client spending remains
cautious, reflecting geopolitical tensions, inflationary pressures and shifting technology priorities.
Selective discretionary spend also tempered the usual Q2 seasonal growth.
Against this backdrop, the key outcomes for the quarter were -
External Document © 2026 Infosys Limited 3
Revenue growth was below our expectations, while AI first revenue now accounts for 10.5% of our
revenues. Operating margin was at 21%. Free cash flow was at $928 mn, representing 113% of net
profit, large deal wins were at $5.2 bn with 62% net new.
Let me now turn to performance drivers and what it means for our outlook.
Q2 revenues were $5,145 mn, an increase of 1.2% sequentially and 1.5% on YoY in constant
currency terms. Acquisition contributed approximately 0.4% to sequential growth. Growth was below
our expectations, volumes were softer and price increases were lower than anticipated amidst high
competitive intensity.
Q2 AI revenue is now 10.5% of total revenue with strong sequential growth of over 29%. Clients are
expanding enterprise wide AI adoption and we are investing in Topaz capabilities and partnerships
to support this opportunity.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
to support this opportunity.
H1 revenue growth was at 1.9% in constant currency terms and 2.1% in reported terms.
We won 19 large deals in Q2 with a TCV of $5.2 bn, which is second highest quarterly TCV in the
last five years. Of this, 62% was net new. This includes an entirely net new $2 bn plus seven year
mega deal with a financial services client. Transition is expected to begin in the second half of Q4.
This deal is expected to contribute over 1% growth for the company in FY28. We also renewed a $1
bn mega deal with an existing financial services client.
Vertical wise, we won seven deals in Financial Services, five in Manufacturing, two each in
Communications, EURS, Life Sciences and one in Hi-Tech. Region-wise, we signed nine deals each
in North America and Europe and one in Rest of the World. This takes H1's total large deal wins to
$8.8 bn, which is a YoY growth of 28% with 62% net new. This will lay a solid foundation for future
growth.
Q2 operating margins were at 21%, decline of 0.1% sequentially.
Major components of the changes are as below:
Headwinds of
- 70 bps from sequential change in post-sales customer support,
- 20 bps additional impact from acquisitions due to one month of additional consolidation,
offset by tailwinds of
- 40 bps of rupee depreciation,
External Document © 2026 Infosys Limited 4
- 20 from Project Maximus and

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
- 20 from Project Maximus and
- 20 bps from higher calendar and working days
Additionally, normalization of 40 bps impact from EURS program terminated in Q1 was offset by
lower realization due to high competitive intensity.
For H1, operating margin stood at 21% at the midpoint of our guided range.
Onsite mix reduced further to 22.6%, reflecting our sustained efforts to help clients achieve cost
reductions. For H1, onsite mix was down by 0.7%. Utilization, including trainees improved by 0.5%,
sequentially to 85.4%, demonstrating continued operational focus. Utilization, excluding trainees
decreased to 81.9% due to fresher intake.
Net headcount increased by about 4,400 employees. We hired about 13,000 freshers in H1 in line
with our target of approximately 20,000 for FY27.
As mentioned last quarter, we are rolling out compensation hikes to most of our employees effective
October '26, with the next phase effective January '27. Attrition reduced to 12.7% versus 13%
sequentially.
We expect effective tax rate for the year to be in the range of 29% to 30%.
Q2 yield on cash investment balance was at approximately 6.9%.
DSO for the quarter was 64, down by seven days compared to DSO last year. DSO, including unbilled
net of unearned was 77 days, down by 10 days as compared to last year.
Free cash flow generation was strong at $928 mn at 113% of net profit. We ended the quarter with

chunks.text:
Free cash flow generation was strong at $928 mn at 113% of net profit. We ended the quarter with
cash and cash equivalents at $4.7 bn and a debt-free balance sheet.
EPS for the quarter stood at `19.32, up 8.7% on a Y-on-Y basis. H1 EPS stood at `38.51, a double-
digit growth of 11.7%.
The Board has announced an interim dividend of `26, an increase of 13% compared to last year.
Coming to verticals,
We had robust large deal signings in Financial Services of more than $3.5 bn in Q2 and saw growth
momentum across global and regional banks, cards and payments, capital markets and Europe.
Mortgage sector is expected to see a slowdown due to increased rate hike expectation. Clients are
prioritizing modernization and AI initiatives focused on cost efficiency and enhanced customer
External Document © 2026 Infosys Limited 5
experience. They are also increasingly moving from AI experimentation to enterprise wide adoption
with Infosys being the preferred AI partner across vast majority of our top clients. While geopolitical
and interest rate uncertainty continues to drive cautious spending, strong deal wins and a healthy
pipeline positions us well for sustained growth.

Middle East conflict, inflation and tariffs are constraining discretionary spend and extending decision

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
Middle East conflict, inflation and tariffs are constraining discretionary spend and extending decision
cycles. Competitive intensity remains high, particularly around AI led productivity commitments. We
are helping clients navigate uncertainty by driving initiatives across supply chain visibility, more
efficient factories and better process. Clients are relooking at the partners across the value chain,
leading to vendor consolidation opportunities.
EURS segment continues to see stable demand with client spending concentrated on targeted, high
impact programs rather than broad based discretionary initiatives. Cost optimization, vendor
consolidation, core modernization and AI led transformation remains key priorities. While competitive
intensity remains high, we are investing in sales and domain capabilities and leveraging differentiated
AI led solutions to improve conversions. Large deal pipeline has grown significantly in last one year,
which provides future growth visibility.
Sequential growth in Retail segment was primarily impacted by lower third-party revenues.
Additionally, subdued environment and macro uncertainty resulted in soft consumer demand, which
has led to ramp-downs in some clients. Consumer tech and Logistics are most impacted on account
of supply chain disruptions. However, there are opportunities around large cost take-outs as well as

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Jayesh Sanghrajka
chunks.text:
of supply chain disruptions. However, there are opportunities around large cost take-outs as well as
transformation programs towards AI. Expectations for AI-led productivity commitments are
increasing competitive intensity and reshaping commercial model.
Communications segment is witnessing a challenging demand environment with clients maintaining
tight control over discretionary spend and prioritizing cost efficiency. AI led driven productivity
expectations are putting pressures on pricing and delivery model. While cost take-outs and vendor
consolidations remain the primary drivers, some opportunities are emerging in transformation, legacy
modernization and AI-led program. We are strengthening domain capabilities and execution speeds

chunks.text:
Hi-Tech segment was impacted by lower third-party revenues as well as reduced spend in a few
large clients due to cost pressures emanating from budget cuts. Clients remain focused on cost
control with hardware spending constrained by macro uncertainties.
We are revising our full year revenue growth guidance to 1% to 2%, reflecting softer-than-expected
H1 performance and our updated assessment for the rest of the year. The lower end assumes further
External Document © 2026 Infosys Limited 6

European manufacturing client and the shift towards offshore delivery remains broadly unchanged.

softer revenue seasonality, continued sharing of AI driven productivity benefits and ramp-up of large
deals. These headwinds will be partly offset by initiatives under Project Maximus.

and a strong large deal pipeline with few mega deals provide a solid foundation for future growth.

way he has built it, the way he has crafted it in terms of the clients he has worked with, in terms of
the people he has worked with.
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 3
And there is a tremendous set of opportunities from that on to the overall company, the learnings
from that as we apply to the overall company. Ashiss Dash, also a very collaborative individual
working well with all of the various components within Infosys and having been here for a long time,
has made sure he has learned everything and also understood how all different parts of the company
work. So huge, huge congratulations to him and looking forward to working with him as we do the
transition over the next few months.

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Rishi Basu
chunks.text:
Rishi Basu
I now invite Jayesh to join Salil on stage to commence the quarter updates. As always, for this
section, I will request one question from each media house. But with that, let me invite Salil for his
remarks. Over to you, Salil.

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
Thanks, Rishi, and thanks Nandan. So good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for being here.
Our revenue growth for Q1 was at 2.4% Y-on-Y and 1% Q-on-Q in constant currency terms. We had
a one-time revenue impact of a client decision during the quarter. Our AI services revenue was 8.2%
of overall revenue in Q1. Our large deals, $3.6 bn at 61% net new, operating margin at 21.1%, free
cash flow at $955 mn. Earnings per share were up 15% Y-on-Y in rupee terms.
We saw a strong acceleration in our AI work, as I shared earlier, with AI revenues at 8.2%. This is
growing at double-digit Q-on-Q for the last several quarters. With this momentum, we see long-term
relevance of our services for our clients, which are all driven through AI. From our delivery team,
over 80,000 employees are working on coding tools such as Claude Code or Codex or several others
for our clients, for our work inside. We see strong traction across the six areas of new growth that
we see in AI, our Hexagon for AI strategy.
We see client work, for example in building agents for processes, work on data, modernization and
using coding tools. We are building a team of frontier engineers to support our client work. Our plan
is to have 6,000 Frontier Engineers over the next few years. We have built a platform, Topaz Fabric

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
is to have 6,000 Frontier Engineers over the next few years. We have built a platform, Topaz Fabric
that enables our clients to get the benefits of AI while keeping the sovereignty of their own data within
their company.
Our clients are able to work with any foundation model, closed, open-weight or on the cloud on their
own servers. Our clients are able to optimize token cost, which has become very critical now to make
sure its appropriate for the type of work they are doing and not out of hand.
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 4
Overall, we continue to see the macro environment remaining uncertain. With our Q1 results and a
view for the rest of the financial year, we are changing our revenue growth guidance to 1.5% to 3%
Y-on-Y growth in constant currency terms. Our operating margin guidance remains the same at 20%
to 22% operating margin.
Thank you. And with that, let's open it up for questions.

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Rishi Basu
chunks.text:
Rishi Basu
Thank you, Salil. We will now open the floor for questions. The first question is from Ritu Singh from
CNBC TV18.

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Ritu Singh
chunks.text:
Ritu Singh
Thank you very much. I know you have asked for one question. But if I may, Salil, you have given
us a big news in this quarter. To begin with, since you speak about how you brought in and Mr.
Nilekani spoke about how you brought in calmness at a time when the company was going through
quite a bit.
Even now you are speaking of this global uncertainty because of which you have had to, again, pull
down your guidance as well. Why decide to leave at a time like now, instead of perhaps looking at
an extension? I wanted to understand. And with the new CEO coming in, any mandate for the new
CEO that you could highlight for us more clearly? And perhaps that is something the investors would
also want to know?
And then on the earnings, of course, the reason for this revision downwards, if you could give us a
little more colour on what you are seeing in the environment, where is the weakness? Where is
momentum picking up?
Some of your competitors like Tech M have been talking about irrational competitive pricing. Wipro
has also spoken about that a bit. So what are you seeing in the environment? And with a 1% kind of
growth in the first quarter, do we assume the second half will be meaningfully better if you were to
reach that upper end of the 3% guidance you are speaking about?
And just on AI, if you could update us how the revenue is moving? Is it proceeding as per what your

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Ritu Singh
chunks.text:
And just on AI, if you could update us how the revenue is moving? Is it proceeding as per what your
expectations were? Any updates you could share on that front as well, as far as revenue contribution
from AI is concerned?

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So let me start with the first one.
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 5
I think you had that question collectively for some time now. We have the answer. As I look at it, I am
really delighted with the role I have played here. We have taken the business, as Nandan said from
$10 bn to $20 bn. It is working very well, the digital transformation and now the AI transformation is
launched. So, I am really delighted that it is working well with our clients and with an incredible team
that we have inside. So that is what I would like to say on the first one.
On the second, I think what we are seeing is an environment, where a little bit sort of combining the
third piece as well, AI services is growing extremely well, double-digit growth, if you look at it like Q-
on-Q, if you look at it over several quarters in the past. We see that those 6 areas that we have
identified like the process, the agents, the data, the engineering, all of those are working extremely
well with our clients. So we are now looking at revenue growth in each of those areas.
Our pipeline is even larger than the 8%, which is the revenue today. So we see good traction in that.
Therefore, we feel there is a good long-term relevance of our services to our clients because this is
going to continue to grow as we look out into the future.

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
going to continue to grow as we look out into the future.
Now the question on the guidance, we had a one-time impact that I shared with a client decision.
There are factors related to what is going on in the macro environment, which we talked about. There
are factors related to the volumes in the quarter. But we look at the large deal number, $3.6 bn, 61%
net new, so we see a lot of support in that. I think there are 5 (Editor’s comment) of those deals
which are consolidation deals that we have been the beneficiary in, as an example. There are 3
(Editor’s comment) deals which are just under the $500 mn range. So just like a mega deal. So we
see really good traction. The pipeline there is looking good.
So all that when we balance, we decided to look at our guidance in a different way. The upper end
of the guidance was really based on if the macro was improving, we now see the macro, it may
improve, but not at the level that we were thinking initially. And so that is how we really constructed
the guidance. But we have tremendous view that this is a good place for Infosys to operate, with AI
the way it is looking and all of the work that we are doing on large deals gives us continued traction.

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Ritu Singh
chunks.text:
Ritu Singh
[Inaudible]. The question of why you didn’t decide to stay on and what the mandates are and you
know better. If you could clarify all of those points?

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So there I think, as I shared earlier, my sense is, I have been fortunate to have a tremendous
opportunity and what we have done in Infosys over the last many years and having taken the
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 6
business from about $10 bn to $20 bn. So it is been an incredible journey. And that with the team
we have and with the client work we have done, that is been a fantastic outcome.
On the mandate, I think as AI strategy is put together, and Dash has been part of that, our thinking
is the strategy we want to execute on. Of course, there will be some things which we will look at in
terms of fine-tuning but that is a natural course of evolution. But the strategy is very well in place to
make sure that it goes into the next phase, making sure the partnerships we have with the various
models, the Topaz Fabric that we built. Today on AI, it is important that clients see that their own data
remains sovereign to them. And the way we built Topaz Fabric, it allows the clients to do that no
matter which model they are using. And that is a very big differentiator we have. For example, in AI,
the token cost that will be an important factor we think in the future.
And we have built Topaz Fabric in a way that, depending on the task you are using the foundation
model for, it will use the right model. So you do not have to pay for the most simple task like an

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
model for, it will use the right model. So you do not have to pay for the most simple task like an
expensive token cost and so on. So we think we are in good position in that.
In terms of second half, first half, I think we have the guidance for the full year. We expect the normal
seasonality that will come. We are not expecting anything unusual there.

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Ritu Singh
chunks.text:
Ritu Singh
Competitive pricing in the market that some of your peers have spoken about?

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Rishi Basu
chunks.text:
Rishi Basu
Thanks Ritu. The next question is from Reshab Shaw from Moneycontrol.

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Reshab Shaw
chunks.text:
Reshab Shaw
Salil, if you could tell us your biggest achievement and what will you miss the most and what is next
coming for you? On the quarterly performance, how has been the TCV conversion because that is
a worry that investors have? And the third question is, two of your peers have highlighted that AI
revenue is slightly lumpy and it could be 1 or 2 quarters post which you will have to go and get those
deals again. So is that something that Infosys is also seeing?

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
So let me start with the second one, I will come back to the first.
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 7
On TCV conversion, we see a pretty good way of converting now. What tends to happen is like,
when you have a consolidation deal, the conversion comes a little bit quicker. When you have a
transformation deal, it is a little bit spread out, but that is the normal sort of conversion we see. We
do not see that it has suddenly changed like in the last quarter or a couple of quarters or so on.
On the AI revenue, I think it is moving so quickly that it is a bit up and down on a quarter-by-quarter
basis. So our thought is, that is why we are saying like look at over the last several quarters, we see
that double-digit type of growth Q-on-Q.
And we will see sometimes it could be a little bit faster but it is growing nonetheless, meaning if you
look at the secular trend, we see that is pretty strong, and that gives us a view that long term, there
is a relevance of what we are doing on AI for the clients.
For me, I think, I am very focused on what we have to do here at Infosys. We have a lot of things to
get done. I want to make sure we remain in the leadership position. We win in the market, we are
leading in AI and I get a smooth transition done. So that is really my focus. And after that, I will see
what else happens.

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Mansee Dave
chunks.text:
Mansee Dave
Hello, good afternoon, Salil and Jayesh. Nice talking to you. Salil, my questions are on client
spending, large deals and competitive positioning. So talking about the client spending, client
budgets remain selective across industries. Have you started seeing any improvement in
discretionary technology spending? Or are enterprises still prioritizing cost optimization over

So how confident are you that these deals will convert into faster revenue growth?
Also, every global IT company today is talking about AI. What would you say is Infosys' biggest

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
Okay. There were a few, so I will start the first was a conversion of the TCV discussion. We see that
the large deals, we see a good traction of those values over the last few quarters have been strong,

External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 8
there is a benefit of the consolidation that we are seeing in some of the large deals, which is definitely
helping us as we go through it.
The conversion, whether it is faster or slower, I think it is at the same type of a level and we will
convert those into revenue with 61% net new, it already looks pretty strong in terms of the net new

On AI, I think there is a huge differentiation that I find from what we are working on. First, we have a

Jayesh has shared in the past, he will share also today, we have invested in building out AI capability.
We have, as I shared earlier, 8% revenue, growing double-digit Q-on-Q over the last several
quarters. We have a good pipeline in that area. Then you look at some of the stats, we have 80,000
people working on the tools today for client work. It is not just training and so on.

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
people working on the tools today for client work. It is not just training and so on.
Then what we built with Infosys Topaz Fabric, I feel is very differentiated because it allows clients to

different models, and lower cost. We have a harness through which they can leverage what they
want to achieve with the foundation model. So that is a significant move up in terms of differentiation

I think in terms of values, my sense has always been Infosys has incredible values and it has really

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Rishi Basu

And secondly, there is also a concern with Vanguard and Daimler and a lot of other companies are

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Salil Parekh
chunks.text:
Salil Parekh
External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 9
So, in GCC, in fact, my sense is you might have seen that we launched an AI GCC concept some

We do not externally share the milestone, but our revenue growth is good. Our work with them is

chunks.text:
Shilpa Phadnis

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Shilpa Phadnis
chunks.text:
